NNS Stack

Source: R/Stack.R
NNS.stack.Rd

Prediction model using the predictions of the NNS base models NNS.reg as features (i.e. meta-features) for the stacked model.

Usage

NNS.stack(
  IVs.train,
  DV.train,
  IVs.test = NULL,
  type = NULL,
  obj.fn = expression(sum((predicted - actual)^2)),
  objective = "min",
  optimize.threshold = TRUE,
  dist = NULL,
  CV.size = NULL,
  balance = FALSE,
  ts.test = NULL,
  folds = 5,
  order = NULL,
  method = c(1, 2),
  stack = TRUE,
  dim.red.method = "cor",
  pred.int = NULL,
  status = TRUE,
  ncores = NULL,
  seed = 123L,
  .validation = NULL
)

Arguments

IVs.train

a vector, matrix or data frame of variables of numeric or factor data types.

DV.train

a numeric or factor vector with compatible dimensions to (IVs.train).

IVs.test

a vector, matrix or data frame of variables of numeric or factor data types with compatible dimensions to (IVs.train). If NULL, will use (IVs.train) as default. Columns are matched to (IVs.train) by name when the two share the same predictor names, and positionally when they share no names at all (as in cbind(test.x_1, test.x_2) against cbind(x_1, x_2)). A column renamed in place, with every other name at its training position (as when read.csv reads a byte-order mark into the first header), is also matched positionally. Names that otherwise only partly overlap the training predictors are ambiguous and return an error.

type

NULL (default) automatically classifies factor, character, logical and two-valued numeric responses. Set type = "CLASS" for nominal classification of any numeric labels, or type = "REG" to fit a numeric response as regression regardless of its number of distinct values. Forecasting calls use type = "REG".

obj.fn

expression; expression(sum((predicted - actual)^2)) (default) Sum of squared errors is the default objective function. Any expression() using the specific terms predicted and actual can be used.

objective

options: ("min", "max") "min" (default) Select whether to minimize or maximize the objective function obj.fn.

optimize.threshold

logical; TRUE (default) Optimizes the threshold for the second first-observed class in binary classification; multiclass decisions use the largest class probability. If FALSE, returns 0.5.

dist

options:(NULL, "NNS", "L1", "L2", "FACTOR") the method of distance calculation. dist = NULL is the default and selects the native blended NNS distance; dist = "NNS" is an explicit alias for the default. dist = "L2" selects Euclidean distance; dist = "L1" selects Manhattan distance; dist = "FACTOR" uses a frequency.

CV.size

numeric [0, 1]; NULL (default) Sets the holdout size for repeated holdout cross-validation (one random holdout per fold). With CV.size = NULL and folds > 1, (stratified, for classification) k-fold cross-validation is used; with CV.size = NULL and folds = 1, a single holdout of random size between 0.2 and 0.33 is used.

balance

logical; FALSE (default) Uses both up and down sampling to balance the classes. type="CLASS" required.

ts.test

integer; NULL (default) Sets the length of the test set for time-series data; typically 2*h parameter value from NNS.ARMA or double known periods to forecast.

folds

integer; folds = 5 (default) Select the number of cross-validation folds.

order

options: (integer, "max", NULL); NULL (default) Sets the order for NNS.reg, where (order = "max") is the k-nearest neighbors equivalent, which is suggested for mixed continuous and discrete (unordered, ordered) data.

method

numeric options: (1, 2); Select the NNS method to include in stack. (method = 1) selects NNS.reg; (method = 2) selects NNS.reg dimension reduction regression. Defaults to method = c(1, 2), which will reduce the dimension first, then find the optimal n.best.

stack

logical; TRUE (default) Uses dimension reduction to select actual predictor coordinates for the multivariate neighbour search; the dimension-reduction component separately uses its synthetic index. If FALSE, both components use their own full predictor designs.

dim.red.method

options: ("cor", "NNS.dep", "NNS.caus", "equal", "all") method for determining synthetic X* coefficients. (dim.red.method = "cor") (default) uses Spearman rank correlation for weights. (dim.red.method = "NNS.dep") uses NNS.dep for nonlinear dependence weights, while (dim.red.method = "NNS.caus") uses NNS.caus for directional association weights. (dim.red.method = "all") averages all methods for further feature engineering.

pred.int

numeric [0,1]; NULL (default) Returns the associated prediction intervals with each method.

status

logical; TRUE (default) Prints status update message in console.

ncores

integer; value specifying the number of cores to be used in the parallelized subroutine NNS.reg. If NULL (default), the number of cores to be used is equal to the number of cores of the machine - 1.

seed

Optional integer random seed used for reproducible resampling, fold construction, and stochastic fitting steps. If `NULL`, the current random-number-generator state is used.

.validation

Internal forecast-validation contract, normally NULL. A list with IVs.train, DV.train, IVs.test, and DV.test supplies the single chronological validation fold when ts.test is set, folds = 1, and CV.size = NULL. It requires exactly N-ts.test training rows and one through ts.test held-out rows; this allows scoring only observed future targets. Training prefixes and generated validation predictors must be constructed without later data. Used only for regression tuning; numeric two-level responses remain regression when this contract is supplied with type = NULL. The final model still fits all original training observations.

Value

Returns a vector of fitted values for the dependent variable test set for all models.

  • "NNS.reg.n.best" returns the optimum "n.best" parameter for the NNS.reg multivariate regression; when all regression points (for classification, all cells) are selected, their number in the final fit. NA for a single predictor in regression, whose univariate NNS.reg fit has no n.best to tune (use cbind(x, x) to search one), and when method does not include 1. "SSE.reg" returns the SSE for the NNS.reg multivariate regression.

  • "OBJfn.reg" returns the best obj.fn value of the NNS.reg regression's tuning on the out-of-fold predictions; it is selection-optimized, not an estimate of out-of-sample performance.

  • "NNS.dim.red.threshold" returns the coefficient cutoff at which NNS.reg on (IVs.train, DV.train) with the same dim.red.method keeps the tuned number of predictors: the smallest kept coefficient magnitude, or 0 when every predictor is kept. Ties at the cutoff keep every tied predictor. For classification it is one number when every class index shares the cutoff, as two-class indices always do, and otherwise one cutoff per class, which NNS.reg accepts as threshold. NA when method does not include 2.

  • "NNS.dim.red.variables" returns the names of the predictors carried by the final dimension reduction regression, ranked by absolute coefficient. With (stack = TRUE) these are also the only predictors used by the NNS.reg multivariate regression, so they are exactly the variables behind "stack". NULL when method does not include 2.

  • "NNS.dim.red.coefficients" returns the named final dimension reduction coefficients for every encoded predictor column (zero for predictors not selected). NULL when method does not include 2.

  • "OBJfn.dim.red" returns the best obj.fn value of the NNS.reg dimension reduction regression's tuning on the out-of-fold predictions; it is selection-optimized, not an estimate of out-of-sample performance.

  • "probability.threshold" returns the optimum probability threshold for classification, else 0.5 when set to FALSE.

  • "reg" returns NNS.reg output.

  • "reg.pred.int" returns the prediction intervals for the regression output.

  • "dim.red" returns NNS.reg dimension reduction regression output.

  • "dim.red.pred.int" returns the prediction intervals for the dimension reduction regression output.

  • "stack" returns the output of the stacked model.

  • "pred.int" returns the prediction intervals for the stacked model.

  • "weights" returns the weights of "reg" and "dim.red" in "stack". For classification they are proportional to the squared "OBJfn.reg" and "OBJfn.dim.red" (inverse squares when objective = "min"); for regression the weight is selected by obj.fn on the out-of-fold predictions of the blend.

Details

Classification tunes and combines class-probability vectors from the NNS predictor cells, preserving nominal label identity. probabilities, reg.probabilities, and dim.red.probabilities return the final probability matrices. Class balancing resamples the training rows of each fold. The neighbour count and the dimension count are chosen by optimizing obj.fn on the pooled out-of-fold predictions; the default classification objective is accuracy. As in NNS 13.0, the two models' probability vectors are then blended with weights proportional to their squared objective scores (inverse squares when objective = "min"), so models with nearly equal scores are blended nearly equally, and the binary probability threshold is tuned on the out-of-fold predictions of that blend. OBJfn.reg and OBJfn.dim.red are the best scores of that search on the same predictions, so they are selection-optimized and overstate held-out performance; assess the final model on an independent test set. Custom objectives receive original numeric or logical response values, and factor/character codes as identified by class.levels. Relabelling is invariant for label-invariant objectives such as accuracy; a custom loss assigning different costs to classes can deliberately change the result.

Named numeric dimension-reduction coefficients are matched to encoded predictor names in both regression and classification. Factor columns use predictor__level names; unnamed vectors follow encoded column order. Classification dimension reduction uses one signed index per class indicator. Its reported coefficients are a list of class-specific equations. The tuned dimension count is returned as NNS.dim.red.count, and NNS.dim.red.threshold gives the coefficient cutoff that keeps that count in every class index: one number when the class indices share it, as two-class indices always do, and otherwise one cutoff per class. The field NNS.dim.red.variables is the union of their active encoded columns. These equations describe the synthetic indices, not a complete saved prediction model: reconstruction also requires training-fitted scaling, the predictor cells, their class frequencies, and the selected smoothing controls. With stack = TRUE, the multivariate classification component retains the selected number of actual encoded coordinates ranked by maximum class-indicator dependence. Prediction.set contains classes attaining the requested estimated probability mass. Binary interval fields contain the range of this set for compatibility; multiclass interval fields are NULL. The sets do not assert calibrated coverage.

For regression, all dimension-reduction coefficients, normalizations, and candidate predictions used in validation are fitted to the corresponding training fold. The final coefficients and regressions are refitted to the full supplied training data. Method 1 retains the selected predictor coordinates, while method 2 evaluates their signed synthetic index; the components can therefore represent different regression geometry.

Note

  • Incorporate any objective function from external packages (such as Metrics::mape) via NNS.stack(..., obj.fn = expression(Metrics::mape(actual, predicted)), objective = "min")

  • Like a logistic regression, the (type = "CLASS") setting is not necessary for target variable of two classes e.g. [0, 1]. Numeric class values are returned on their original scale; factor and character responses use codes with the returned class.levels mapping.

  • Missing data should be handled prior as well using na.omit or complete.cases on the full dataset.

References

Viole, F. (2016) "Classification Using NNS Clustering Analysis" doi:10.2139/ssrn.2864711

Author

Fred Viole, OVVO Financial Systems

Examples

 ## Using 'iris' dataset with a stratified test set of ten rows per species
 ## (rows 141:150 alone are all virginica).
 if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
 test.set <- c(41:50, 91:100, 141:150)
 NNS.stack(iris[-test.set, 1:4], iris[-test.set, 5], IVs.test = iris[test.set, 1:4],
 type = "CLASS", balance = TRUE)

 ## Using 'iris' dataset to determine [n.best] and [threshold] with no test set.
 NNS.stack(iris[ , 1:4], iris[ , 5], type = "CLASS")
 } # }
